items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: And let's see, I don't know if they were in the band at that time, but at one time the trumpet players were Bill Coleman and Frank Newton.

ctx.x: Did Charley Johnson's band -- I'm not -- I don't know about it, so, did it have interesting soloists also?

Well, they -- let's put it this way, it was a swinging band for that era. They had a drummer, I can't remember his last name, his name was George something, he was just excellent. And let's see, I don't know if they were in the band at that time, but at one time the trumpet players were Bill Coleman and Frank Newton. And it was, oh, I guess they had -- well, it was just like two trumpets and a trombone and three saxophones and four rhythm. It wasn't, you know, one of those huge bands. But none of the bands were…

items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: We found out that his name was Charlie Barnet... It was after I knew him at the Strand Ballroom that he formed a band which played in a big hotel down town.

ctx.x: Very often, a young fellow used to come to the Strand but he never danced and spent most of his time in the dressing room that we had next to the bandstand. Sometimes

he would be high and go to sleep in a chair until he became a little sober. We found out that his name was Charlie Barnet and that he was from a rich family. But it was some years later when Charlie took a band in to one of the big white hotels that I found out that he was a musician. He talked with us at the Strand but I don't remember him ever mentioning that he played sax. He really must have liked Neal's band because he came so often and spent his time in our dressing room.

Horace Henderson had a band playing in the Dunbar Palace which had been called Bamboo Inn when I first came to New York. It was a small dance hall on 7th Avenue between 139th and 140th Streets. He was using two trumpets, Gus McClung and Jack Butler, when he decided to add another trumpet. Gus left the band after Horace hired the other trumpet and I joined the band.
